page.layout: One block of running text: a Latin poem in italic verse lines in one column, below the running head and page number. A decorative fleuron stands below the poem and is not text.

p.i: Atque meis renuunt feroces Parere iußis. Ecce cadentium Tingam refuso spicula sanguine, Nostraque casorum vorabunt Tela manu iaculata carnes. Monstrabo victor splendidus hostium Tergo retortos brachia principes Clarisque deductos triumphis Excidio perimam cruento. O, festa lato pectore gaudia Plebes redempta ducite. Nam Deus Mortes suorum vindicabit, Iamque potens properabit vltor Iustis Tyrannos tundere cladibus: Turbasque tandem proteret hosticas Simul sacrata gentis omne Lethiferum scelus expiarit.

page.notes: The poem's lines are set with indents, but no clear stanza break is visible, so the whole poem is given as one paragraph; the first word "Atque" is a fragment continuing from the previous page. Spelling was normalised per rule: the initial I of "Iustis", "iußis", "Iamque" and "iaculata" is written J, and "vltor" is written "ultor". Long s is plain s throughout. The decorative fleuron below the poem is not transcribed.
